nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis of V₆O₁₃ nanobelts
nodes.procedure: V₆O₁₃ nanobelts were prepared using a simple solvothermal method with the addition of H₂O and C₂H₅OH as solvents. Via the reduction of C₂H₅OH, commercial V₂O₅ nanoblocks were successfully transformed into V₆O₁₃ nanobelts (Figure S1a and b).
nodes.source_text: First, V₆O₁₃ nanobelts were prepared using a simple solvothermal method with the addition of H₂O and C₂H₅OH as solvents... (Figure S1a and b)

nodes.name: Room temperature in-situ conversion to V-PBA
nodes.procedure: Under the effects of H⁺ from glacial acetic acid (0.0175 M) and diluted HCl solution, vanadium ions were released from V₆O₁₃ nanobelts ([H⁺] = 0.0044 mol L⁻¹ initially, then 0.0101 mol L⁻¹). Finally, free vanadium ions formed V-PBA nanocubes after addition of K₃Fe(CN)₆ ligand at room temperature without noble gas protection. The obtained V-PBA materials was green.

nodes.source_text: Herein, we report for the first time an environmentally friendly and mild in-situ generation and conversation strategy for preparing uniform V-PBA nanocubes using V₆O₁₃ nanobelts as the vanadium source... at room temperature without the protection of noble gas

nodes.description: CV measurements of V-PBA cathode in AZIB (aqueous zinc-ion battery)
nodes.source_text: Figure 3a displays the cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements of V-PBA conducted in the operating voltage range of 0.2 - 2.0 V. In the first three cycles, the V-PBA exhibited three pairs of reduction/oxidation peaks at 0.75 / 0.53 V, 1.08 / 0.89 V, and 1.75 / 1.56 V, corresponding to the reversible electrochemical reactions of V³⁺-V⁴⁺, V⁴⁺-V⁵⁺, [Fe(II)(CN)₆]⁴⁻-[Fe(III)(CN)₆]³⁻

Figure 3b exhibits the galvanostatic charge/discharge (GCD) curves of the V-PBA at a current density of 0.1 A g⁻¹. The electrode just exhibited a discharge specific capacity of around 56 mA h g⁻¹ before activation and reached more than 200 mA h g⁻¹ in the 5th cycle

The V-PBA electrode can exhibit discharge specific capacities of 210.6, 68.9, 62.6, 56.2, and 50.6 mA h g⁻¹ at current densities of 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, and 1.0 A g⁻¹, respectively. Moreover, the materials retained a specific capacity of 57.3 mA h g⁻¹ upon return of the current density to 0.1 A g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: V-PBA displayed typical type-IV N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms and possessed a high specific surface area of 183 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area and corresponding Barrett-Jouner-Halenda pore size distribution curves can be seen from Figure 1j and k. The V-PBA displayed typical type-IV N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms and possessed a high specific surface area of 183 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows peaks at ~2100 cm⁻¹ and ~2150 cm⁻¹ from Fe(III)-C≡N and Fe(II)-C≡N stretching vibrations, confirming V-PBA framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We observed a gradual increase in the magnitude of the peaks at ∼2100 cm⁻¹ and ∼2150 cm⁻¹, which can be attributed to the stretching vibration of Fe(III)-C≡N and Fe(II)-C≡N groups in the V-PBA framework

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows enhanced peak at 2100 cm⁻¹ representing C≡N, confirming V-PBA formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The same conclusion can be arrived at upon examination of Raman spectra (Figure 2g), the enhanced peak at 2100 cm⁻¹ represents for C≡N, which illustrates the successfully formation of V-PBA.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of both V⁴⁺ (516.1 eV 2p₃/₂, 523.2 eV 2p₁/₂) and V⁵⁺ (517.2 eV 2p₃/₂, 524.5 eV 2p₁/₂) with V⁴⁺ decreasing and V⁵⁺ increasing during conversion; Fe³⁺ at 710.3 eV and 724.1 eV; enhanced O 1s peaks at 533.1 eV and 531.5 eV from absorbed and crystal water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the V 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 2i), the peak intensity of V⁴⁺ 2p₃/₂ at 516.1 eV and 523.2 eV in V⁴⁺ 2p₁/₂ have an downward tendency while the V⁵⁺ at 517.2 eV in V⁵⁺ 2p₃/₂ and 524.5 eV in V⁵⁺ 2p₁/₂ possess a upward tendency. This suggests that the amount of V⁴⁺ gradually increase and the prepared V-PBA have both V⁵⁺ and V⁴⁺. In the Fe 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 2j), we observed that the Fe³⁺ 2p₃/₂ and Fe³⁺ 2p₁/₂ peaks at 710.3 eV and 724.1 eV, respectively, indicating Fe³⁺ was reduced by V⁴⁺. In the O 1s XPS spectrum (Figure 2k), ... the pure V-PBA possess a significantly enhanced peak at 533.1 and 531.5 eV, which belong to the absorbed water and crystal water, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ XRD shows peaks at ~35° (400) and ~16.8° (200) shift to lower angles upon Zn²⁺ insertion and return upon extraction, with no new peaks indicating no phase change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ XRD test was performed to explore the Zn²⁺ storage mechanism of the V-PBA cathode... Figure 5a and b shows the peaks located at ∼35° and ∼16.8° corresponding to the (400) and (200) crystal planes, which shifted to lower angles upon the insertion of Zn²⁺ but returned to their original state upon the extraction of Zn²⁺. Notably, no new peaks appeared during the charge/discharge process

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex-situ XPS shows Zn 2p peaks at 1021.7 eV (2p₃/₂) and 1044.6 eV (2p₁/₂) appear upon discharge to 0.2 V indicating Zn²⁺ insertion, weaken upon recharge to 2.0 V; V⁴⁺ peaks increase on discharge, V⁵⁺ decrease; Fe²⁺ converts to Fe³⁺ on discharge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis was conducted to study the surface elements and electronic states of the V-PBA cathode during the first discharge and charge processes... When discharged to 0.2 V, two distinct peaks appeared at 1021.7 and 1044.6 eV corresponding to Zn²⁺ 2p₃/₂ and Zn²⁺ 2p₁/₂, respectively; this result indicates the successful insertion of Zn²⁺ into the V-PBA cathode. When recharged to 2.0 V, the peak density of Zn²⁺ weakened... In the V 2p spectrum shown in Figure 5g, peaks located at 515.4 and 516.7 eV (V 2p₃/₂), and 523.1 and 524.2 eV (V 2p₁/₂) can be attributed to V⁴⁺ and V⁵⁺, respectively. As shown by these results, the peak intensities associated with V⁴⁺ increased when discharged to 0.2 V and decreased when recharged to 2.0 V
